clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old man with a strong family history of breast cancer presented with right breast pain, nipple retraction, and skin induration. Mammography revealed a high-density, irregularly shaped retroareolar mass with spiculated margins, and associated nipple and skin retraction (E002). Ultrasound confirmed a 1.4 cm solid, hypoechoic, irregular retroareolar mass (E003). A punch biopsy showed invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast with epidermal involvement, which was ER+, PR+, and HER2+ (E001). Staging PET/CT did not show nodal or distant metastatic disease (E004). The patient underwent a modified radical mastectomy, and the sentinel lymph node biopsy was positive for metastatic carcinoma, leading to a full axillary dissection (E005).

Staging PET/CT scan did not show nodal or distant metastatic disease.
Patient underwent modified radical mastectomy; sentinel lymph node biopsy was positive for metastatic carcinoma, followed by full axillary dissection.
